Looking at the cuboid (3×2×2), the visible cubes are:
- **Gray:** the entire top-front row (3 cubes) plus the bottom-front-left cube → 4 cubes, so the gray piece is complete (an L-shape).
- **Dark:** bottom-front-middle, bottom-front-right, bottom-back-right → 3 cubes, needing one hidden cube.
- **White:** the entire top-back row (3 cubes), needing one hidden cube.

The two hidden cubes are the bottom-back-left and bottom-back-middle. If the dark piece took the bottom-back-left cube, it would be disconnected from the rest of the dark cubes. So the dark piece must include the bottom-back-middle cube (forming a 2×2 square), leaving the **bottom-back-left cube for the white piece**.

Therefore the white piece is a row of three cubes with one cube attached below the end — an L-shape. Among the options, this matches diagram B (a column of three with one cube at the end).
